content.text: National Science, Technology and Innovation Policies, Premier Research Institutions, and Eminent Indian Scientists

India's scientific and technological enterprise is anchored in a succession of national policy frameworks designed to foster self-reliance, indigenous technological capability, and socio-economic transformation. From post-independence institution-building under Jawaharlal Nehru to contemporary initiatives in frontier technologies, science and technology serve as the principal instruments for national development.

content.text: 1. Evolution of National Science, Technology & Innovation Policies

content.caption: Comparative Analysis of India's S&T Policy Frameworks
rows: Scientific Policy Resolution (SPR), 1958
Drafted under PM Nehru and Homi Bhabha; emphasized pure scientific research, cultivating 'scientific temper' (Article 51A(h)), and training elite scientific manpower.
Establishment of IITs, national research laboratories under CSIR, atomic energy research, and premier universities.
Technology Policy Statement (TPS), 1983
Promoted technological self-reliance, import substitution, and absorption of imported technologies during the non-aligned era.
Strengthened indigenous industrial R&D, domestic capital machinery design, and reduced reliance on foreign technology licenses.
Science and Technology Policy (STP), 2003
Integrated S&T into post-1991 market liberalization; emphasized public-private partnerships (PPP) and increased national R&D gross expenditure.
Expansion of biopharmaceutical R&D, software technology parks, and intellectual property rights (IPR) management.
Science, Technology & Innovation Policy (STIP), 2013
Positioned India among the top global scientific superpowers; coined 'Science for People' and faster inclusive innovation for rural and MSME development.
Birth of Atal Innovation Mission (AIM), Startup India ecosystem, BIRAC biotechnology incubation, and space commercialization.
Draft STIP 2020 / National Research Foundation (NRF) Act 2023
Decentralized, evidence-informed policy; 'Open Science' policy (One Nation One Subscription); mainstreaming traditional knowledge; boosting Gross Expenditure on R&D (GERD) to 2% of GDP.
Establishment of Anusandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF) with ₹50,000 crore corpus to fund academic and industrial research across universities.

content.text: 2. Premier Scientific Research Institutions in India & Andhra Pradesh

content.caption: Premier National and Regional Scientific Institutions
rows: CSIR (Council of Scientific & Industrial Research)
Ministry of Science & Technology (Autonomous, 1942)
Network of 37 national laboratories; includes CCMB (Hyderabad/AP border) for genomics, IICT for chemical technologies, and NGRI for geophysics.
ICAR (Indian Council of Agricultural Research)
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare (1929)
Apex agricultural research body; Green Revolution pioneer; operates CTRI (Central Tobacco Research Institute) in Rajahmundry, IIOPR (Oil Palm) in Pedavegi, AP.
ICMR (Indian Council of Medical Research)
Ministry of Health & Family Welfare (1911)
Biomedical research apex; led COVID-19 vaccine trials (Covaxin); operates NIV Pune, and National Institute of Nutrition (NIN).
ISRO / SDSC SHAR Sriharikota
Department of Space (Govt of India)
Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC SHAR) in Tirupati district, AP; India's sole operational spaceport featuring First and Second Launch Pads for PSLV, GSLV, and LVM3.
DRDO (Defence Research & Development Organisation)
Ministry of Defence (1958)
Missile systems, naval sonars, radar technologies; operates NSTL (Naval Science & Technological Laboratory) in Visakhapatnam, AP.

items: Sir C.V. Raman (1888–1970): Discovered the Raman Effect (inelastic scattering of photons by molecules) on 28th February 1928 (celebrated as National Science Day); awarded the 1930 Nobel Prize in Physics; founded the Raman Research Institute.

Dr. Homi J. Bhabha (1909–1966): 'Father of the Indian Nuclear Programme'; formulated India's unique Three-Stage Nuclear Power Programme; founded Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR) and Trombay Atomic Energy Establishment (now BARC).

Dr. Vikram Sarabhai (1919–1971): 'Father of the Indian Space Programme'; established Physical Research Laboratory (PRL) and INCOSPAR (which evolved into ISRO); spearheaded the SITE (Satellite Instructional Television Experiment) in 1975.

Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam (1931–2015): 'Missile Man of India'; Project Director of India's first satellite launch vehicle (SLV-3); architect of Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme (IGMDP: Agni, Prithvi); 11th President of India.

Srinivasa Ramanujan (1887–1920): Mathematical genius; profound contributions to analytical number theory, infinite series, continued fractions, elliptic functions, and mock theta functions (National Mathematics Day on 22nd December).
Satyendra Nath Bose (1894–1974): Theoretical physicist; developed Bose-Einstein Statistics and predicted the Bose-Einstein Condensate; eponym of fundamental subatomic particles known as 'Bosons'.

Sir M. Visvesvaraya (1860–1962): Renowned civil engineer and statesman (Engineers' Day on 15th September); engineered automatic sluice gates at Khadakwasla, Krishna Raja Sagara dam, and flood protection systems for Hyderabad and Visakhapatnam port.

Dr. Yellapragada Subbarow (1895–1948): Andhra-born biochemist (from Bhimavaram); discovered the role of ATP (Adenosine Triphosphate) as the cellular energy currency, synthesized Methotrexate (first anticancer chemotherapy drug), Aureomycin (tetracycline antibiotic), and Hetrazan (cure for filariasis).

content.text: Part A: Mains Analytical & Descriptive Questions

items:
Trace the evolution of Science, Technology and Innovation (STI) policies in post-independence India. How does the Anusandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF) Act, 2023 aim to revolutionize R&D funding? (APPSC Group-1 Mains, 10 Marks)
-> Model Approach: Trace chronological evolution: SPR 1958 (scientific temper, higher education), TPS 1983 (self-reliance), STP 2003 (market integration, PPP), STIP 2013 (inclusive innovation), and Draft STIP 2020; analyze India's persistent R&D deficit (Gross Expenditure on R&D stagnant at ~0.65% of GDP compared to 2-3% in US/China); detail the structure of ANRF: ₹50,000 crore budget over 5 years (with ~70% targeted from private industry philanthropy/investments); explain how ANRF democratizes research grants across state universities beyond elite IITs/IISc.

Highlight the contributions of Dr. Yellapragada Subbarow to medical biochemistry and pharmacotherapy. Why is he celebrated as one of India's greatest unsung scientists? (APPSC Group-1 Mains, 10 Marks)
-> Model Approach: Introduce Dr. Yellapragada Subbarow hailing from Bhimavaram, West Godavari, Andhra Pradesh; detail his groundbreaking discoveries at Harvard and Lederle Laboratories: Fiske-Subbarow method for phosphorus estimation, isolation of ATP and phosphocreatine (vital for muscle contraction and cellular energy); explain his synthesis of Methotrexate (foundation of modern cancer chemotherapy) and aminopterin; detail the discovery of Aureomycin (first broad-spectrum tetracycline antibiotic saving millions of lives) and Hetrazan (diethylcarbamazine for curing lymphatic filariasis); conclude with his lasting legacy in global pharmacology.

Evaluate the strategic role of Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC SHAR), Sriharikota in India's space program and its technological significance for Andhra Pradesh. (APPSC Group-1 Mains, 10 Marks)
-> Model Approach: Describe the geographical advantages of Sriharikota island in Tirupati district: coastal location allowing rockets to launch eastward over the Bay of Bengal (using Earth's rotational boost and ensuring debris falls into ocean), proximity to the equator; detail launch infrastructure: First Launch Pad, Second Launch Pad, Solid Propellant Booster Plant (SPROB), and integration facilities; discuss historic missions launched from SHAR (Chandrayaan-1/2/3, Mars Orbiter Mission, Aditya-L1, PSLV-C37 carrying 104 satellites); analyze regional economic and educational spillovers in Andhra Pradesh.

content.text: Part B: Screening / Prelims Objective Questions

items:
Q1. National Science Day is celebrated in India on February 28 every year to commemorate which landmark discovery?
(a) Discovery of Zero by Aryabhata
(b) Discovery of the Raman Effect by Sir C.V. Raman
(c) Launch of Aryabhata satellite
(d) Pokhran-I Nuclear Test
Correct Answer: (b) Discovery of the Raman Effect by Sir C.V. Raman [Explanation: February 28 marks the day in 1928 when Sir C.V. Raman discovered the Raman Effect, which earned him the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1930.]

Q2. The Anusandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF) Act, enacted by Parliament in 2023, replaces which existing statutory research body?
(a) CSIR (Council of Scientific and Industrial Research)
(b) SERB (Science and Engineering Research Board)
(c) ICMR (Indian Council of Medical Research)
(d) TIFAC
Correct Answer: (b) SERB (Science and Engineering Research Board) [Explanation: The ANRF Act 2023 repeals the Science and Engineering Research Board Act, 2008 and subsumes SERB into ANRF.]

Q3. Which eminent scientist from Andhra Pradesh synthesized Methotrexate (the first anti-cancer drug) and discovered the cellular energy role of Adenosine Triphosphate (ATP)?
(a) Dr. Yellapragada Subbarow
(b) Dr. A.S. Rao
(c) Sir C.V. Raman
(d) Dr. Suri Bhagavantam
Correct Answer: (a) Dr. Yellapragada Subbarow [Explanation: Dr. Yellapragada Subbarow (born in Bhimavaram, AP) was a pioneering biochemist who discovered ATP and synthesized Methotrexate and Aureomycin.]

Q4. Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC SHAR), the primary space launch centre of ISRO, is located in which district of Andhra Pradesh?
(a) Nellore
(b) Tirupati (formerly part of SPSR Nellore)
(c) Prakasam
(d) Chittoor
Correct Answer: (b) Tirupati (formerly part of SPSR Nellore) [Explanation: Sriharikota is located in the newly carved Tirupati district (post-2022 district reorganization of Andhra Pradesh).]

Q5. Subatomic particles that have integral spin (0, 1, 2) and follow Bose-Einstein statistics are named 'Bosons' in honour of which Indian scientist?
(a) Homi J. Bhabha
(b) Satyendra Nath Bose
(c) Jagadish Chandra Bose
(d) Meghnad Saha
Correct Answer: (b) Satyendra Nath Bose [Explanation: Paul Dirac coined the term 'Boson' to honor Indian theoretical physicist Satyendra Nath Bose for his pioneering work on quantum statistics.]
